para: The duality structure of the graph is particularly revealing. Paraconsistency and paracompleteness — properties that have historically been treated as independent and competing departures from classical logic — appear in the graph as a pair of symmetric positions with respect to the duality operations of . A paraconsistent calculus is one in which the principle of explosion (⊥ ⊢ φ for arbitrary φ) fails; its dual under δL is a paracomplete calculus, one in which the principle of excluded middle (⊢ φ ∨ ¬φ) fails. The graph makes this duality structural and explicit: it is not a philosophical observation about two families of non-classical logics, but a theorem about the action of a specific operation on a specific class of sequent calculi. Identifying the duality makes it possible to transfer results across the paraconsistent–paracomplete divide automatically, and to identify the precise metalinguistic conditions that define membership in each family.
